questions.stem: The main problem of trade by barter is

options.text: the existence of too much money in circulation
the high rate of interest charged by banks
the issue of notes by the Central Bank

questions.explanation: Barter requires each trader to want exactly what the other is offering at the same moment. That double coincidence is rare in a large market, which is why a generally acceptable medium of exchange developed. Other barter problems, such as indivisibility, follow from the same lack of money.

distractorRationale.b: Too much money is a problem of inflation, which can exist only after money has already been introduced
distractorRationale.c: Interest rates belong to a money-using banking system, not to barter
distractorRationale.d: Note issue is a function of a central bank and is irrelevant to a moneyless exchange

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of money?
questions.explanation: A store of value is something money does: it lets purchasing power be held over time. Portability, durability and divisibility are qualities that make a commodity suitable to serve as money, not functions. Examiners set this trap every year.

distractorRationale.a: Portability is a quality of good money, not a function
distractorRationale.b: Durability is a quality — notes and coins must not wear out quickly
distractorRationale.d: Divisibility is a quality that lets money make change; it is not a function

questions.stem: Currency in circulation is ₦200 billion, demand deposits are ₦300 billion and savings deposits are ₦400 billion. What is M2, in billions of naira?
questions.explanation: M1 equals currency plus demand deposits, which is 200 + 300 = ₦500 billion. M2 is M1 plus savings and time deposits, so 500 + 400 = ₦900 billion. Savings deposits are part of broad money but not of narrow money.

questions.stem: According to Keynes, the speculative demand for money

options.text: rises as the rate of interest rises
falls as the rate of interest rises
is independent of the rate of interest
depends only on the level of national income

questions.explanation: When interest rates are high, bonds and interest-bearing deposits are attractive, so people hold less idle cash for speculation. When rates are low, the opportunity cost of holding money is small and the chance of a future rate rise (which would cut bond prices) is larger, so speculative balances increase.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the relationship; a higher interest rate raises the opportunity cost of idle cash
distractorRationale.c: The speculative motive is the one Keynes tied most closely to the interest rate
distractorRationale.d: Income mainly determines the transactions and precautionary motives, not the speculative motive

questions.stem: A salary that is agreed today and paid at the end of the month illustrates money acting as a
questions.explanation: A contract that names a future payment in naira uses money as a standard of deferred payment. The same naira will later serve as a medium of exchange when the salary is spent, but the function illustrated by agreeing the sum now and paying later is the deferred-payment function.

distractorRationale.a: The medium-of-exchange function is the act of buying goods, not the act of contracting to pay later
distractorRationale.c: Token coin describes the form of metallic money, not a function
distractorRationale.d: Commodity money is an early form of money, such as cowries, not a function

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly traces the evolution of money?

options.text: Paper money → commodity money → metallic money → bank deposits
Barter → commodity money → metallic money → paper money → token and deposit money
Bank deposits → metallic money → barter → paper money
Token coins → barter → cowries → gold coins

questions.explanation: Exchange began as barter, then used commodities such as cowries and salt, then metals that could be coined. Paper notes followed as receipts for metal and later as fiat money; modern systems add token coins and bank deposits. Any sequence that starts with paper or deposits skips the earlier stages.

distractorRationale.a: Paper money cannot precede commodity and metallic money historically
distractorRationale.c: Bank deposits are a late development, not the starting point, and barter comes first rather than after metals
distractorRationale.d: Token coins are modern small change; they cannot precede barter and commodity money

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a quality of good money?
questions.explanation: Good money must have qualities such as durability, divisibility, and scarcity. Perishability is a disadvantage as it means the money can lose its value over time.

distractorRationale.a: Durability is essential as money must withstand physical wear and tear.
distractorRationale.b: Divisibility allows money to be broken into smaller units for transactions.
distractorRationale.c: Scarcity ensures that money retains its value by being limited in supply.
